stem: \(\underline{\text{Noticing}}\) the change in the behaviour of the officer, the cadets returned to their position.

Target word: 'Noticing'.
It is the -ing form of the verb 'notice', it heads the phrase 'Noticing the change in the behaviour of the officer', and that whole phrase describes the subject 'the cadets'.
A verb form used in this way, doing the work of an adjective while keeping an object of its own, is a participle; it is not a present continuous because there is no auxiliary 'are' with it.

stem: When he reached the department, the officials \(\underline{\text{had left}}\) for the meeting.
solution:
Target words: 'had left'.
The form is 'had' plus the past participle 'left'.
That form shows an action completed BEFORE another past action ('when he reached the department'), which is the past perfect.
A plain past tense would be 'left' on its own.
Matches option A.

stem: He \(\underline{\text{has offered}}\) her another chance.
solution:
Target words: 'has offered'.
The form is 'has' plus the past participle 'offered'.

Matches option C.
context: Directions: part of speech of the underlined word
reviewNote: TWO DEFENSIBLE ANSWERS. 'has offered' is in the perfect tense AND is transitive (it carries the objects 'her' and 'another chance'), and both labels are printed. Keyed on the tense axis because the underline covers the auxiliary as well as the participle, which is what makes the FORM the point - compare Q26 ('had left' - Past perfect verb), while the transitivity items in this paper (Q19 'fought', Q49 'won') underline the lexical verb alone. Worth adjudicating.

stem: The building \(\underline{\text{is}}\) very ancient.
solution:
Target word: 'is'.
Ask 'is WHAT?' - there is no object; 'very ancient' is an adjective phrase describing the subject, not something the verb acts upon.
A verb that takes no object is intransitive; such linking verbs are treated as intransitive verbs of incomplete predication.
It is not an auxiliary here, because there is no other verb for it to help - it is the main verb of the sentence.
Matches option B.
context: Directions: part of speech of the underlined word
reviewNote: JUDGEMENT CALL. 'is' here is the copula: it is the MAIN verb and takes no object, so 'intransitive' is the grammatically defensible label (Wren and Martin file verbs of incomplete predication under intransitive verbs). Some keys loosely call the copula an auxiliary or linking verb, which is the rival reading, but nothing here is being helped by it. Worth adjudicating.

stem: He is \(\underline{\text{the}}\) most sought after teacher in the school.
